name: mouse-mover-impl
description: Design, implement, review, build and test a CGO-free Windows Mouse Mover Go app, cross-compiled from WSL Fedora.

steps.prompt:
Create a git worktree for the Mouse Mover build. The repo is in WSL Fedora. Run this exact command from PowerShell:

wsl -d FedoraLinux-44 -- bash -lc 'cd /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover && git worktree add .worktrees/mouse-mover-impl -b feature/mouse-mover-impl main'

The base branch is `main`. After creating it, confirm the worktree exists by listing /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover/.worktrees/mouse-mover-impl. All later steps operate in that worktree.

IMPORTANT: git must run inside WSL (the Windows host reports 'dubious ownership'). Report success or the exact error.

Author requirements and a technical design document for a Windows desktop app 'Mouse Mover' written in Go. Write the design to the file (UNC path for your file tools) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\docs\DESIGN.md (create docs/ if needed).

CRITICAL ENVIRONMENT (do not re-investigate; trust these): The repo is in WSL Fedora. Go 1.26.8 and gcc are installed INSIDE WSL; the Windows host has NO Go and NO C compiler, and there is NO mingw-w64. Therefore the ENTIRE app MUST be pure Go with CGO_ENABLED=0 so it cross-compiles to windows/amd64 from Fedora. Fyne and any CGO/OpenGL GUI library are FORBIDDEN. All commands run via `wsl -d FedoraLinux-44 -- bash -lc 'export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin:/usr/lib/golang/bin; cd /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover/.worktrees/mouse-mover-impl && <cmd>'`. For editing source/doc files use the file tools against the UNC path \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\... (PowerShell mangles heredocs, so never create files via the shell).

The design must cover, with concrete decisions (not open questions): module path github.com/jarvis/mouse-mover; package layout cmd/mousemover, internal/winapi (CGO-free Win32 bindings for SendInput/GetCursorPos/SetCursorPos and virtual-screen multi-monitor metrics via golang.org/x/sys/windows, with //go:build windows real files and //go:build !windows stub files so the module tests on Linux), internal/engine (cancellable mover: context.Context, time.Ticker, goroutine, sync.Mutex+running guard against duplicate Start, immediate Stop, last-move time + elapsed, depends on a Mover/CursorController interface so it is unit-testable on Linux with a fake), internal/config (JSON settings under %LOCALAPPDATA%\MouseMover\settings.json, Validate for interval bounds + pattern enum, defaults, round-trip Load/Save), internal/ui (native Win32 CGO-free main window + system tray; window shows app name, status, Start/Stop, interval presets 30s/1m/2m/5m/custom, movement pattern selector, last-move time, elapsed; tray minimize + menu Show/Start/Stop/Exit + active/inactive indication + clean engine shutdown on exit; UI behind //go:build windows with a !windows stub so the Linux-testable packages still build), build/ (build.sh cross-compile, package.sh portable ZIP, a non-elevated per-user installer), README.md. Also cover the no-admin constraints (no UAC/service/HKLM, portable + %LOCALAPPDATA% install) and a LIMITATIONS section (UIPI/Secure Desktop/locked session/group policy can block synthetic input; interactive GUI/tray/SendInput only verifiable on real Windows). Resolve the GUI/tray approach concretely: a single Win32 message loop on the main OS thread (runtime.LockOSThread) driving a window + Shell_NotifyIcon tray icon, all CGO-free; if any third-party systray helper is proposed it MUST build with CGO_ENABLED=0 for windows/amd64.

If a prior iteration left findings in \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.agents\tasks\design-review.json, address every finding and revise DESIGN.md.

Review the technical design at (UNC path) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\docs\DESIGN.md for the Mouse Mover Go app. Check for ambiguity, gaps, unverified assumptions, and especially: does every component have a concrete CGO-free design (no Fyne/CGO), is the engine genuinely unit-testable on Linux via an interface + fake, do the build tags let the config/engine packages build and test on Linux while isolating Windows-only UI code, and are the no-admin and verification constraints addressed. Any HIGH or MEDIUM finding blocks.

Write your verdict as JSON to the file (UNC path for your file tools) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.agents\tasks\design-review.json with exactly this shape: {"verdict": "APPROVED" | "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "findings": [{"severity": "HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW", "note": "..."}]}. Set verdict to APPROVED only when there are no HIGH or MEDIUM findings. Create the .agents/tasks directory if needed.

Produce an ordered implementation plan for the Mouse Mover Go app from the APPROVED design at (UNC path) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\docs\DESIGN.md. Write the plan to \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\docs\PLAN.md.

The plan must sequence the work so the Linux-testable core (config, engine with its Mover interface + fake, winapi stubs) comes before the Windows-only UI, and so go.mod/go mod tidy pulls golang.org/x/sys early. Preserve the verification contract: the final validation runs go vet ./..., go test ./..., a windows/amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 cross-compile, and the packaging scripts. Do not change the review-state file contract used by the build loop (code-review writes verdict to .agents/tasks/code-review.json). All commands run inside WSL Fedora with PATH including /usr/local/go/bin; source files are edited via the UNC path with file tools (PowerShell mangles heredocs).

Implement the Mouse Mover Go app in the worktree per the plan at (UNC path) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\docs\PLAN.md and the design at docs/DESIGN.md.

CRITICAL ENVIRONMENT (trust, do not re-investigate): repo is in WSL Fedora. Run Go/git ONLY inside WSL: `wsl -d FedoraLinux-44 -- bash -lc 'export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin:/usr/lib/golang/bin; cd /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover/.worktrees/mouse-mover-impl && <cmd>'`. Go is at /usr/sbin/go, GOROOT=/usr/lib/golang, GOPATH=/home/jarvis/go. The Windows host has NO Go/C compiler and there is NO mingw — so the whole app MUST be pure Go, CGO_ENABLED=0, cross-compiling to windows/amd64. NO Fyne, NO CGO, NO OpenGL. Edit ALL source files with the file-editing tools against the UNC path \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\...  — NEVER create files through the shell (PowerShell mangles heredocs). Keep every WSL shell command single-line in single quotes; for multi-step sequences write a .sh script with the file tools and run it via `wsl -d FedoraLinux-44 -- bash /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover/.worktrees/mouse-mover-impl/<script>.sh`.

Requirements to satisfy (all of them): module github.com/jarvis/mouse-mover; run go mod tidy inside WSL to populate golang.org/x/sys. internal/winapi CGO-free SendInput/GetCursorPos/SetCursorPos + virtual-screen multi-monitor metrics (GetSystemMetrics SM_?VIRTUALSCREEN) with //go:build windows real files and //go:build !windows stubs. internal/engine cancellable goroutine (context + time.Ticker), sync.Mutex+running guard so repeated Start is a no-op, immediate Stop, captures cursor -> minimal configurable movement -> restores original position -> clamps to virtual-screen bounds, never moves while stopped, tracks last-move time + start time; engine uses a Mover/CursorController interface so it is unit-testable on Linux with a fake. internal/config Settings + Load/Save JSON under %LOCALAPPDATA%\MouseMover\settings.json + Validate (interval bounds, pattern enum) + defaults. internal/ui native Win32 CGO-free window (app name, status, Start/Stop, interval presets 30s/1m/2m/5m/custom, pattern selector, last-move time, elapsed) + system tray (minimize to tray, menu Show/Start/Stop/Exit, active/inactive indicator, clean engine shutdown on exit) using a Win32 message loop on the main OS thread (runtime.LockOSThread) + Shell_NotifyIcon; UI behind //go:build windows with a !windows stub so config/engine still build and test on Linux. cmd/mousemover/main.go wires everything. No admin: no UAC/service/HKLM, portable + per-user %LOCALAPPDATA% install, no protected-dir writes, no unnecessary permissions, running state always visible, no keyboard simulation, immediate Stop. Handle Windows API errors (check SendInput return / GetLastError).

Tests REQUIRED (must run on Linux via go test ./...): config validation (valid/invalid intervals, pattern enum, round-trip Load/Save) and engine scheduling (ticker fires, Stop cancels promptly, duplicate Start no-op, capture-move-restore via fake Mover, clamp to bounds). Add //go:build windows integration tests where practical (skipped on Linux).

build/build.sh: `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "-H windowsgui -s -w" -o dist/MouseMover.exe ./cmd/mousemover`. build/package.sh: portable ZIP with MouseMover.exe + README. A non-elevated per-user installer (.ps1 or .bat) copying to %LOCALAPPDATA%\MouseMover + Start Menu shortcut, no UAC. README.md: setup, build & test (exact WSL cross-compile command), usage, portable vs per-user install, troubleshooting, uninstall, LIMITATIONS (UIPI/Secure Desktop/locked session/policy block synthetic input; GUI/tray/SendInput only verifiable on real Windows).

Before finishing: run inside WSL `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, and `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "-H windowsgui -s -w" -o dist/MouseMover.exe ./cmd/mousemover`; fix everything until all three are green and dist/MouseMover.exe exists. Then run build/build.sh and build/package.sh. Write a verification report to \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl\docs\verification.md capturing the exact commands and their output (test results, exe size, zip path). Commit all work on branch feature/mouse-mover-impl with clear messages (git inside WSL).

If \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.agents\tasks\code-review.json exists with findings from a prior iteration, address EVERY finding, re-run the three gate commands, update verification.md, and commit.

Review the Mouse Mover implementation on branch feature/mouse-mover-impl in the worktree at (UNC path) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl. Read the diff, the source, and the evidence in docs/verification.md. Run git/go commands inside WSL: `wsl -d FedoraLinux-44 -- bash -lc 'export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin:/usr/lib/golang/bin; cd /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover/.worktrees/mouse-mover-impl && <cmd>'`.

Verify behaviorally, not just by reading: (1) `go vet ./...` passes; (2) `go test ./...` passes on Linux and genuinely covers config validation and engine scheduling (duplicate-Start no-op, immediate Stop, capture-move-restore, clamp to bounds) — not trivial stubs; (3) `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "-H windowsgui -s -w" -o /tmp/MouseMover-check.exe ./cmd/mousemover` compiles cleanly (proves the full Windows build including UI/winapi/tray is CGO-free and sound); (4) the code is pure Go / CGO-free (no Fyne, no import \"C\"), the engine never moves while stopped, Start cannot create duplicate loops, movement clamps to virtual-screen bounds and restores the cursor, settings validate and round-trip, and the no-admin constraints hold (no HKLM/service/UAC). Flag missing LIMITATIONS docs or missing packaging scripts.

Do NOT require runtime verification of the interactive GUI/tray/SendInput motion — that is impossible in this headless Linux environment and is expected to be deferred to real Windows; only require that it COMPILES for windows/amd64 and that the testable logic passes.

Write your verdict as JSON to (UNC path) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.agents\tasks\code-review.json with exactly: {"verdict": "APPROVED" | "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "findings": [{"severity": "HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW", "file": "...", "note": "..."}]}. Set APPROVED only when the gate commands pass and there are no HIGH or MEDIUM findings. This issues-only report is the final word of the iteration.

Final fail-closed validation gate for the Mouse Mover app in the worktree at (UNC path) \\wsl.localhost\FedoraLinux-44\home\jarvis\repos\mouse-mover\.worktrees\mouse-mover-impl. Run everything inside WSL Fedora: `wsl -d FedoraLinux-44 -- bash -lc 'export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin:/usr/lib/golang/bin; cd /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover/.worktrees/mouse-mover-impl && <cmd>'`.

Run, in order, and REPORT THE ACTUAL OUTPUT of each:
1. go vet ./...
2. go test ./...  (must pass on Linux)
3. GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "-H windowsgui -s -w" -o dist/MouseMover.exe ./cmd/mousemover  (must produce dist/MouseMover.exe; report `ls -la dist/MouseMover.exe` size)
4. bash build/build.sh and bash build/package.sh (must produce the portable ZIP; report its path and `ls -la`)

If ANY command fails, FIX the code (edit via UNC file tools) and re-run until all are green. A command exiting 0 is the only acceptable evidence. Commit any fixes on feature/mouse-mover-impl.

Then integrate: rebase the feature branch onto main (do NOT try to move main — it is checked out in the user's main worktree, so git will refuse; only rebase here):
`wsl -d FedoraLinux-44 -- bash -lc 'cd /home/jarvis/repos/mouse-mover/.worktrees/mouse-mover-impl && git fetch && git rebase main'` (resolve any conflicts; if none, this is a no-op). Ensure the branch is committed and clean.

Finally send a concise completion summary via your notification: the test results, the dist/MouseMover.exe size, the ZIP path, and an explicit statement that the interactive GUI/tray/SendInput behavior was COMPILED for windows/amd64 and unit-tested logic passes on Linux, but was NOT runtime-verified because this is a headless Linux build environment and requires running MouseMover.exe on a real Windows 10/11 host. Report success only if gates 1-4 are green.
